items.title: Chevron Pays a Bigger Dividend, but Exxon May Be the Better Retirement Stock
items.summary: One oil giant hands retirees a bigger check today, while the other has kept raising its payout through every crash. When crude collapses again, which dividend will you wish you owned?

items.title: Why Chevron Investors Could Make Sense Of ETFs Now
items.summary: You might like Chevron for its global energy reach, but owning the stock directly means carrying its specific risks by yourself. Simply Wall St highlights one of those: that earnings are forecast to decline an average of 5.2% per year over the next 3 years. Holding Chevron through a fund that also owns other businesses spreads how much those company specific issues can swing your portfolio, and also spreads out how much its success can help you. The dividend currently appears covered at about US$65 Brent per barrel.
